description: Rajas con Crema is a beloved Mexican vegetarian dish featuring smoky roasted poblano peppers bathed in a rich, creamy sauce. Sweet corn kernels add a delightful texture and sweetness, making it an incredibly flavorful and comforting side or main. This versatile recipe brings the authentic taste of Mexico right to your table, perfect for any meal.

instructions.title: Roast and Prepare Poblanos
instructions.text: Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame, on a comal, or under a broiler until the skin is charred and blistered on all sides. Place the hot peppers immediately into a plastic bag or covered bowl to steam for 10-15 minutes. Once cooled, peel off the charred skin, remove the stems and seeds, then slice the flesh into thin strips (rajas).

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or comal over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced white onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Corn and Rajas
instructions.text: Stir in the corn kernels and cook for 3-5 minutes, allowing them to lightly brown if desired. Add the prepared poblano strips (rajas) to the skillet and sauté for another 2-3 minutes to combine the flavors.

instructions.title: Create the Creamy Sauce
instructions.text: Pour in the Mexican crema (or thinned sour cream) and whole milk. Stir gently to incorporate all ingredients. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, but do not boil vigorously, as this can cause the crema to curdle.

instructions.title: Melt the Cheese and Season
instructions.text: Sprinkle the shredded Oaxaca cheese over the mixture. Continue to simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the cheese is fully melted and the sauce has slightly thickened, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving. Rajas con Crema is excellent served warm as a side dish with tacos, enchiladas, or as a main course with warm tortillas.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, roast your poblanos directly over an open gas flame or on a hot comal until evenly charred. This imparts a deep smoky flavor that cannot be replicated by oven roasting alone.
If Mexican crema is unavailable, you can substitute with sour cream thinned with a little milk or heavy cream. For a richer sauce, use half-and-half or heavy cream instead of whole milk.
Rajas con Crema is wonderfully versatile. Serve it as a side dish, use it as a filling for quesadillas or enchiladas, or even stir it into scrambled eggs for a hearty breakfast.
